speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are concerned about your infant's bilious vomiting and inability to pass meconium; this is a serious combination of symptoms. Can you tell me exactly how many days old your baby is and when the vomiting started?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia (specifically Distal Ileal Atresia or Jejunal Atresia).

The combination of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium within 24-48 hours, and abdominal distension in a neonate strongly suggests a distal intestinal obstruction. While Hirschsprung's disease and Meconium Ileus are differential considerations, the complete failure to pass meconium at birth often points towards atresia or a distal imperforate anus. I will request an abdominal X-ray to look for the "double bubble" sign or gas distribution patterns to confirm the level of obstruction.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_XRay
